description: Alpha-beta pruning returns the minimax score while it skips moves that cannot change the decision. It carries a window `(α, β)`: `α` is the score *Max* is already sure of elsewhere, `β` the score *Min* is sure of. A side stops searching its moves once its best score reaches the far edge of the window. This version is *fail-soft*: a pruned position returns its best score found, which may lie beyond the window, as a bound. It saves most when good moves come first, so order the moves and try the last principal variation first.

papers.authors: Donald E. Knuth, Ronald W. Moore
papers.title: An analysis of alpha-beta pruning
